_comment: PRE-REGISTERED analysis decisions for the 3-arm x 20-seed study. Frozen BEFORE any evaluation result is computed (sweep launched 2026-07-16; no checkpoint has been evaluated). run_production_eval.py refuses to run confirmatory tests unless signed_off is true - set it only after supervisor agreement, and do not edit values afterwards. Any post-hoc change must be reported as such in the thesis.
signed_off_by: Colin Melville (candidate), 2026-08-27. SUPERVISOR CONFIRMATION: Dr Wen signed off on the pre-registration and on every amendment dated up to 2026-10-06 on 2026-10-07, and on the two amendments of 2026-10-09 on 2026-10-12 (both reported by the candidate). The decisions were taken by the candidate and put to her in the v2 design brief of 2026-08-27; her confirmation came later, and is recorded with its own date so the provenance stays accurate.

equivalence_margins._comment: H2 (no clean-data degradation) TOST margins on the mean paired difference, defended-vs-baseline, attack-off condition. DECIDED 2026-08-27: FIXED margins of 0.5, i.e. option (a). The alternative, 10 percent of the fixed-policy A-S arm's clean-data value, was rejected as degenerate: that arm's mean annualised Sharpe fell near zero (0.119) against a standard deviation of 41.81, so the margin resolved to 0.012 and no equivalence test could ever clear it. That is a property of the BENCHMARK arm alone, which this pre-registration always allowed inspecting without seeing the defended arms, so the choice is not defended-arm peeking - but the sequence is disclosed here and must be disclosed in the writeup. 0.5 is chosen for internal consistency with progression_gate, which already treats 0.5 on this same annualised scale as the tolerable shortfall against the benchmark; the same magnitude is therefore treated as negligible in both places. NOTE ON POWER: at the v1 noise level (seed-level sd 40-58) a 0.5 margin is far inside the standard error, so a non-equivalent verdict is the likely outcome regardless of the true effect. Where TOST is inconclusive the paired difference and its confidence interval are reported as the estimate, and no equivalence is claimed.

sensitivity_axes._comment: Pre-registered sensitivity/ablation sweeps (estimation-only, no confirmatory claims). The telegraph axis was committed to Dr Wen (2026-06 email). CORRECTED 2026-08-26: the symmetric telegraph (attack_on_prob = attack_off_prob = 0.1) gives a ~50% attack-REGIME duty cycle, but the realized positive-label rate is far lower, because adv_label fires on the adversary's ACTION (injected volume > label_floor), not on the regime. Measured over 403 MM updates of a completed config-3 run: mean label rate 0.110, with 57.6% of updates containing NO positive labels at all. The original 'chosen for detection-label balance' justification is therefore not supported by the realized data and must not be repeated in the writeup; the sensitivity sweep tests whether this rate drives the results.
sensitivity_axes.attack_telegraph: attack_on_prob/attack_off_prob in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} (symmetric) plus one asymmetric low-duty setting

interpretation_notes._comment: Pre-registered BEFORE results to prevent post-hoc goalpost moves.
interpretation_notes.absolute_pnl: Absolute MM profitability is NOT a hypothesis: Mohl et al. (2511.02136, Sec 5.2) report their learned MM loses ~0.2 ticks on average yet outperforms the A-S baseline, partly due to the structural price-time-priority disadvantage of per-step re-quoting, which this MM inherits. All H1-H4 claims are comparative (across arms / vs A-S), not absolute.
interpretation_notes.no_trade_equilibrium: The Spooner-family reward is not volume-normalised; Mohl et al. observe near-no-trade optima. quote_presence_(on|off) is reported per arm to make this failure mode visible rather than silently inflating risk-adjusted metrics.
interpretation_notes.observation_space_adversary: The spoofing adversary places NO orders: SpoofingAgent.get_messages returns empty message and cancel arrays, and AdversarialMARLEnv.step_env runs the full LOB step unmodified, then adds the injected volume to a COPY of the L2 snapshot handed to the MM as its observation. Real fills, mid price and PnL are untouched by construction. This is a deliberate model of the informational effect of spoofing (a spoof order is cancelled before execution, so its economic function is to mislead), but it means the attack can only change outcomes VIA the MM's policy response. It must be described in the writeup as perturbing the market maker's observed depth, NOT as manipulating the order book.
interpretation_notes.quote_presence_validity_gate: quote_presence = fraction of steps with a two-sided quote posted (posted_bid_price > 0 AND posted_ask_price > 0). Because the adversary is observation-space only, an MM whose policy is insensitive to its observations is trivially invariant to attack and scores IDENTICALLY under attack-on and attack-off - looking maximally robust for the wrong reason. PRE-REGISTERED DECISION (made 2026-08-26, before the full evaluation was read): an arm whose seeds are predominantly quote_presence ~= 0 cannot support an H1 robustness claim, and any such result is to be reported as policy collapse (the Mohl et al. no-trade failure mode) rather than as robustness. quote_presence and mean_attack_rate are reported per arm and per condition so this is checkable. Observed in a 2-seed pilot (eval_1121620): config-3 quote_presence = 0 with mean_attack_rate_on = 1.0 and every risk metric identical between attack-on and attack-off.

common_adversary._comment: Every arm evaluated under attack faces the config-3 arm's adversary, paired by seed index (internal validity for H1).

periods_per_year_derivation: 2024_test cache: 275,141,175 msgs / 64 days = 4,299,081 msgs/day; at 100 msgs/step -> 42,991 steps/day x 252 trading days = 10,833,681 return-steps/year. Annualisation rescales Sharpe/Sortino uniformly across arms; paired contrasts are invariant to it.
label_materiality_note: 0.0 = any positive injected volume counts as an attack step (legacy behaviour, matches training).
training_schedule_note: All arms trained SINGLE-PHASE on the full 2024-01-01..2024-09-30 pool (22.23 GB message array, uniform window sampling, no calendar-ordered curriculum), 1002 updates x 512 steps x 16 envs, identical across arms; evaluation exclusively on the untouched 2024-10-01..2024-12-31 holdout. CHANGED 2026-08-26 from the earlier chained-quarters (Q1->Q2->Q3) plan: that design existed only to fit a 16 GB V100, and after the GPU partition outage all training moved to CPU nodes with 1.5 TB RAM, where the whole pool fits in one phase. Uniform sampling also removes the curriculum ordering as a confound. All arms use the SAME backend (CPU) - mixing CPU/GPU arms would confound the H1 contrast via float op-ordering.

superseded_runs.v1_config1_baseline / v1_config2_adversa: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-27. Trained and evaluated in full (60 seeds, eval_1136928) but INVALID as a test of H1-H4 because of a bobRL action-space misconfiguration: n_actions=6 was sampled against the bob_v0=1 ladder, which has only 3 entries. JAX clamps an out-of-range gather index to the last element, so actions 3/4/5 all collapsed onto the final one-sided entry (bid=0, ask=2). Four of six actions were sell-only and exactly one quoted two-sided, giving a uniform-policy prior of 1/6 = 0.167 on market making. Observed quote_presence was 0.169 (full), 0.299 (baseline), 0.319 (adversarial) - the full arm was indistinguishable from an untrained policy - with peak_inventory 110-148 against the A-S benchmark's 27 and inventory_sd 31-42 against 8.4. The progression gate FAILED on all three criteria. All contrasts were null after Holm correction, which is uninformative because the three arms shared the same broken action space. The A-S arm was unaffected (action_space=AvSt) and is the reason the fault was visible at all.
superseded_runs._retained_because: The v1 checkpoints and eval_1136928 are KEPT, not deleted. They are the evidence that a pre-registered, benchmark-anchored progression gate and the quote_presence validity metric caught a silent implementation fault that every significance test absorbed without complaint. That is reported as a methodological finding.
superseded_runs._v2_changes: v2_* arms fix the action space to bob_v0=2 with n_actions=5 (a 5-action ladder whose first three entries are two-sided, with bid/ask skew for inventory control; uniform-policy P(two-sided) = 0.6). A constructor assert in mm_env.py now rejects any n_actions that does not match the bob_v0 ladder length. Evaluation episodes per seed raised from 16 to 64 because the deterministic A-S arm showed sharpe_off = 0.119 +/- 41.81 across seeds, i.e. the between-arm comparisons were noise-dominated. softmin_sharpe was made scale-invariant (a fixed softmin temperature on PnL-scale returns produced |values| ~ 3e10). No hypothesis, metric, alpha, margin or seed-count decision was changed.
superseded_runs.v3_v2_arms: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-02. The v2_* arms (6 x 20 seeds, eval_1151304 / eval_1151370, byte-identical reproductions of each other) trained and evaluated in full but FAILED both pre-registered gates. Progression gate FAIL on all three criteria (sharpe -8.80 vs A-S 4.60; sortino 0.24 vs 17.47; inventory_sd 79.32 vs the 16.34 ceiling). Validity gate FAIL: quote_presence bimodal at exactly 0.00 or above 0.3, with 10-14 of 20 seeds per arm never posting a two-sided quote, and every such seed producing bit-identical attack-on and attack-off metrics. Cause diagnosed from the training logs: every env config set auto_liquidate_threshold = 0, which disables the only mechanism that actively reduces inventory, while the bobRL ladder emits only LIMIT orders at the touch. The MM therefore had NO action that reduces a position; inventory ratcheted one way and reward decayed from about -2.5 to -34 across every 6400s episode (sawtooth period 12.50 updates = episode_time/NUM_STEPS = 6400/512). Not quoting was the only way to stop the bleed growing, and it is absorbing, because a policy that never quotes never gets a fill to learn from.
superseded_runs._v3_changes: v3_* arms set auto_liquidate_threshold = 50 on all six bobRL env configs, giving the MM a position limit beyond which inventory is flattened at market via IOC. The key existed but was implemented only in _getActionMsgs_fixedQuant, so on the bobRL path every arm actually runs it was read from config and silently never used; it is now mirrored into _getActionMsgs_BobRL and pinned by tests/test_position_limit.py. Threshold 50 rather than 100 because the progression gate requires inventory_sd <= 2 x A-S's 8.17 = 16.34 and a limit T bounds sd at roughly 0.58 x T. Validated by pilot arrays 1168520 (T=50) and 1168521 (T=100), 6 seeds x 200 updates: no within-episode sawtooth detected, rewards O(-0.1) against v2's O(-45), and 0 of 6 seeds collapsed in either (terminal entropy 0.74-1.19 and 1.08-1.51, unimodal, against v2's bimodal 0.00-0.42 / 1.07-1.57). Not set on the A-S config: AvSt does not implement the key, and A-S holds inventory_sd 8.17 / peak 26, far inside any limit, so it would never bind.

adversary_cost_model._comment: DECIDED 2026-08-27. Enforcement against spoofing is disgorgement of illicit profit, so the regulatory term is a PROFIT TAX rather than a per-share fee: expected cost = p_detect * kappa * max(gross gain, 0), where gross gain is what the adversary extracts from the market maker (-r_mm, floored at zero, entering with a one-step lag). Replaces the earlier per-unit-volume penalty, which is retained in code as reg_cost_mode='volume' for comparison only.
adversary_cost_model.kappa_anchor: SEC v. Lek Securities / Avalon FA (S.D.N.Y. 2019-20): court-ordered disgorgement against Avalon and principals was $4,495,564 plus $131,750 prejudgment interest. Disgorgement is defined as illicit profits, so kappa ~ 1.
adversary_cost_model.p_detect_status: PLACEHOLDER - no published estimate anchors the probability that a given episode's manipulation is detected and pursued. Swept as a sensitivity axis and reported as an assumption, not a calibrated quantity. Enters only as the product with kappa, so the kappa sweep partly absorbs uncertainty in it.
adversary_cost_model.accidental_fill_cost: c_fill = 0.001 on expected filled volume x (half-spread + inverse-depth impact), charged every active step. EXPECTED FILLED VOLUME IS PER-STEP: p_fill(v_t) * v_t, where v_t is the volume posted on that step. A spoof order is posted and cancelled within the step, so its fill risk is a flow. Corrected 2026-08-27 - the implementation had been reading the episode's CUMULATIVE injected volume, which made the cost quadratic and unbounded in it (measured avg_reward_ADV ~ -7.7e6 against an MM reward of order 1). Cumulative volume is still tracked for budget and OTR accounting. This restores the model as specified; it is not a change to it.
adversary_cost_model.unconstrained_comparator: Arm F (v3_config6_unconstrained) sets kappa = p_detect = c_fill = 0, giving the unconstrained spoofer the proposal promises as a baseline. NOTE: every arm of the superseded v1 run had these at zero, so no earlier result exercised the economic constraint at all.

design._comment: Six arms x 20 seeds. B/C/D/E form a 2x2 factorial over {detection head, regime conditioning} so each factor is estimated at both levels of the other - the v1 design confounded them in a single arm. A is the no-adversary reference for H1; F is the unconstrained-adversary comparator for contribution 1.
design.B_adversarial: v3_config2_adversarial: constrained adversary, no MM defences
design.F_unconstrained: v3_config6_unconstrained: unconstrained adversary, no MM defences

amendments.change: auto_liquidate_threshold 0 -> 50 on the six bobRL env configs; arm projects renamed v2_* -> v3_*.
amendments.motivation: Both pre-registered gates failed on v2 because of an environment implementation fault, not because of anything the hypotheses predict. Diagnosed from training logs and two 6-seed pilots BEFORE any v3 checkpoint existed.
amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE. Hypotheses, primary_metrics, alpha, multiplicity, equivalence_margins, progression_gate criteria, seeds, checkpoint_step, periods_per_year and the common-adversary design are all unchanged. This amendment fixes the ENVIRONMENT, not the statistics, which is why signed_off is not reset.
amendments.caveat: The pilots ran 200 updates, a fifth of production, and classified seeds by terminal policy entropy rather than measured quote_presence. They establish that the ratchet is absent at that horizon; they do not establish that the v3 arms clear the progression gate. That remains a genuine pre-registered risk of failure.

amendments.name: v4_spread_skew_amendment
amendments.change: The market maker's action space moves from bobRL (bob_v0=2, a 5-entry ladder varying QUANTITY only, quoting at the touch) to spread_skew, a 2x3 grid over {tight, wide} spread x {bid, neutral, ask} skew that DERIVES quoted prices from mid and the prevailing spread. Arms are renamed v4_*. Everything else - seeds, LR, GAMMA, FREEZE_ALTERNATION, reward function, position limit, adversary and its cost model - is held at the v3 values.
amendments.motivation: v3 (eval 1179095) left H1 close to untestable rather than merely unsupported. The adversary is observation-space only, but _getActionMsgs_BobRL takes prices from world_state - the REAL book - and the ladder varies quantity alone, so a perturbed observation could influence which of five quantity pairs the policy chose and nothing else. The MM's quoted prices were immune to spoofing by construction, which is the likely reason the B-vs-A effect was d = 0.242 with Holm p = 0.939. spread_skew gives the adversary a price lever for the first time. Decided BEFORE any v4 checkpoint existed.
amendments.inference_status: EXPLORATORY. v4 yields effect sizes and confidence intervals only. No confirmatory claim about H1-H4 may be made from v4 under any multiplicity scheme, and no v4 p-value may be reported as a significance result. The CONFIRMATORY RESULT OF RECORD REMAINS v3 (eval 1179095): H1 null, H2 not shown equivalent, H3 null, H4 directional. v4 is reported as a mechanism study of whether giving the adversary a price lever changes the picture, and its role in the thesis is to explain v3, not to replace it.
amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE. alpha, multiplicity, primary_metrics, equivalence_margins, progression_gate criteria, seeds (n=20), checkpoint_step and the common-adversary design are untouched. This amendment changes the AGENT'S ACTION SPACE, not the statistics, which is why signed_off is not reset.
amendments.implementation_notes: spread_skew had not been exercised in this project and carried four defects, all fixed and pinned by tests/test_spread_skew.py (56 tests, both scalar and vmapped shapes): (1) posted_bid_price and posted_ask_price were hardcoded to 0, so quote_presence - the validity gate - would have reported a total quoting collapse in every arm regardless of behaviour, indistinguishable from the real v2 failure; (2) empty_book was hardcoded False, so quantities were never zeroed on an empty book; (3) auto_liquidate_threshold was implemented only in _getActionMsgs_fixedQuant and so was inert on this dispatch path, exactly as it had been on bobRL before v3 - the v3 position limit is now ported here; (4) an unrecognised multiplier_type left skewed_mid undefined. Constructor guards on n_actions == 6 and num_action_messages_by_agent == 2 were added as defence-in-depth; MarketMaking_EnvironmentConfig.__post_init__ already forces both, so they document an invariant rather than fix a live fault.
amendments.behavioural_change_recorded: spread_skew now masks the agent's OWN resting orders before reading the touch, as bobRL already did. This is a change to what the agent does, not only to what it reports, and is recorded as such. It matters more here than in bobRL: bobRL quotes AT the touch, whereas spread_skew derives prices FROM mid and spread, so quoting off one's own resting orders is a feedback loop that walks the quote away from the market. spread_multiplier (3.0), skew_multiplier (5.0) and multiplier_type ('tick') are now written out explicitly in the env config; they were absent from every v1-v3 config and would otherwise take dataclass defaults unnoticed, the same failure mode as inv_penalty_quadratic_factor.
amendments.validity_gate_caveat: quote_presence LOSES ITS DISCRIMINATING POWER under spread_skew and must not be cited as evidence that v4 is valid in the way it was for v3. spread_skew posts fixed_quant_value on BOTH sides on every step, so quote_presence is 1.0 unless the book is empty or the position limit is liquidating. The v2 failure mode it was built to catch - a policy abandoning two-sided quoting - is not expressible in this action space. Validity for v4 must be argued from inventory_sd, peak_inventory and the within-episode reward drift instead.
amendments.preconditions_before_the_sweep: A single-seed smoke run must reach at least update 3 (both previous v4-class launches died inside 80 seconds), and the perturbed-vs-clean action-agreement check must show the adversary actually flipping the selected action. If a spoofed observation does not change the chosen action, v4 fails for v3's reason and the sweep should not be run.

amendments.name: forced_worst_case_attack_amendment
amendments.change: New standalone script eval_forced_attack.py overrides actions[adv_idx] immediately before each env.step in an evaluation rollout, substituting a fixed maximal one-sided injection (all-bid or all-ask) for the co-trained adversary's own policy output, against EXISTING v4 MM checkpoints. No retraining. Budget (budget_per_episode) and telegraph gate (attack_on_prob/attack_off_prob) are overridden uniformly on every arm. Zero changes to adversarial_marl_env.py, spoofing_agent.py, rollout.py, run_evaluation.py or run_production_eval.py.
amendments.motivation: check_adversary_sidedness.py on the v4 common evaluation adversary (v4_config3_full) found it ABSTAINS (mean action 0.159% of max) under its cost model; a cost-free variant (v4_config6_unconstrained's own adversary) attacks at 54% of max but converges to a SYMMETRIC injection (sidedness 0.08/1.0), which cannot move queue_imbalance. Either way H1 is unidentifiable with a co-trained adversary: a null is indistinguishable from MM robustness. See docs/note_h1_attack_effect.md. A forced worst-case perturbation tests MM sensitivity directly, decoupled from whether a rational adversary would choose to exploit it. Decided BEFORE any forced-attack result existed.
amendments.budget_and_gate: CORRECTED IN DRAFTING, before any result: an earlier draft claimed the baseline arm would make a forced attack a no-op because its TRAINING env (adversarial_mm_v4_config1.json) sets budget_per_episode=0.0. That is wrong for evaluation - eval_2024_test_v4_config1.yaml deliberately loads the config-2 env json, and every v4 eval env runs with budget_per_episode=1e6. The gate is forced by set_attack_mode('on') exactly as in the production eval. The budget is still set explicitly on every arm because the trained adversary never tested whether 1e6 sustains a MAXIMAL injection over a full episode; budget_final_frac / budget_exhausted_frac are checked before the grid and the value raised if it binds.
amendments.axes: side in {bid, ask}, both run. Budget override value resolved empirically before the full grid (checked non-binding over a full episode, raised if it binds), not assumed. RESOLVED 2026-09-27 before the grid: 1e6 bound (exhausted in 3.9% of env-steps on the ask side, job 35838); 1e7 did not (job 35875: attack rate 1.000, exhausted 0%, 92.5% remaining). Grid runs at 1e7. Smoke tests also showed the off condition reproducing eval_17313 exactly (max|diff|=0).
amendments.inference_status: EXPLORATORY. Effect sizes and confidence intervals only. Reported as a new, clearly-labelled supplementary robustness analysis; not a rerun of, replacement for, or reconciliation with the v3 confirmatory result (eval_1179095) or the v4 exploratory result (eval_17313), which stand as reported. Output metric keys are suffixed _forced/_off (never _on/_off) so a forced-attack file cannot be mistaken for a co-trained-adversary result.
amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE. alpha, multiplicity, primary_metrics, equivalence_margins, progression_gate criteria, seeds (n=20), checkpoint_step and the common-adversary design of the confirmatory study are untouched.
amendments.preconditions_before_the_sweep: Single-seed smoke test on the BASELINE arm must show mean_attack_rate_forced ~= 1.0 with budget_final_frac well above 0, and its off condition must reproduce eval_17313.json's *_off values for that seed (the forced-attack loop is faithful to the production loop). Single-seed smoke test on the FULL arm must show a |queue_imbalance| shift in the ballpark of check_adversary_lever.py's one-sided reference (~0.50 at inject_mult=2.0), with the signed shift flipping between --side bid and --side ask. If either fails, the override is not reaching the environment as assumed and the grid is not run.

amendments.name: robustness_checks_amendment_2026-09-28
amendments.change: Adds four analyses motivated by docs/literature_audit_2026-09-28.md. None replaces or re-runs a pre-registered test; the confirmatory result of record (v3, eval_1179095), the v4 exploratory result (eval_17313) and the forced-attack result (forced_attack_v4_{bid,ask}) stand as reported. RC1: exact sign-flip permutation test (two-sided, mean paired difference) plus a BCa bootstrap CI on the same estimand, run on the existing per_seed arrays for every contrast those four files already report, Holm-adjusted within the same families as each file's holm block. RC2: Sharpe/Sortino (and sortino_low/highvol, regime_gap) reported in per-step units = annualised / sqrt(periods_per_year); gate and equivalence margins scaled by the same factor, so every verdict, p-value and effect size is unchanged by construction. RC3: detection-head AUROC under the forced maximal one-sided attack, per seed = AUROC of det_prob pooled over the forced (label 1) and off (label 0) conditions, step 0 dropped, for the head arms detection, full, detection_noobs, both sides, budget 1e7, 20 seeds. RC4: effective rank (Roy & Vetterli 2007) and srank_0.01 (Kumar et al. 2021) of the 128-d SharedEncoder output, plus the fraction of dead ReLU units, on one FIXED observation set (clean rollout of v4 baseline seed 0) for every v4 arm x seed checkpoint.
amendments.motivation: Literature audit 2026-09-28: RC1 because the pre-registered Shapiro-Wilk gate distorts conditional error rates (Rochon et al. 2011, 2012) and the bootstrap CI and Wilcoxon p address different estimands; RC2 because sqrt(q) annualisation is valid only for IID returns (Lo 2002); RC3 because AUROC ~0.50 was only ever measured against an adversary injecting ~0.16% of max, so a chance-level score cannot distinguish a head that cannot detect from labels that were noise; RC4 because Moalla et al. (2024) attribute PPO actor collapse to feature-rank loss that auxiliary losses prevent, which is the candidate mechanism for the detection-head effect on collapse.

decision_rules.RC1: The pre-registered test remains the result of record. Every contrast whose verdict at alpha=0.05 differs between the pre-registered test and RC1 is listed in the thesis, in either direction.
decision_rules.RC3: Per arm x side: one-sample test of the 20 per-seed AUROCs vs 0.5 (stats.one_sample_comparison, plus RC1 sign-flip), Holm over the 6 arm x side cells. Mean AUROC >= 0.60 with Holm p < 0.05 -> the H3 chance result is reinterpreted as a label/treatment artefact (the head detects a material attack). 95% CI of the mean inside [0.45, 0.55] -> the head cannot detect even a maximal one-sided attack. Otherwise inconclusive. detection_noobs is included because its head is trained even though its output is not consumed.
decision_rules.RC4: Primary: the three minimal-pair isolations of the head factor, paired by seed index - detection vs adversarial, full vs regime, detection_noobs vs adversarial - on effective rank, RC1 sign-flip p, Holm over 3. Mechanism supported if all three differences are positive and >= 2 of 3 survive Holm. If head arms show no higher rank, the thesis states that the collapse mechanism is NOT feature-rank loss and keeps the head effect as a behavioural finding without a mechanism claim. srank_0.01 and dead-unit fraction are secondary, reported descriptively.

amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE. alpha, multiplicity, primary_metrics, equivalence_margins, progression_gate criteria, seeds (n=20), checkpoint_step and the common-adversary design are untouched. RC1-RC4 are additional reporting.
amendments.written_before_results: Yes. No RC1-RC4 statistic had been computed when this entry was written (2026-09-28). RC3 and RC4 require new Kaya jobs that had not been submitted.
amendments.kappa_anchor_correction: Recorded 2026-09-28; the kappa value (1.0) is NOT changed. kappa_anchor cites the ORIGINAL final judgment's disgorgement ($4,495,564 + $131,750 interest). The amended final judgment of 2021-02-09 (affirmed 2d Cir. 2022-06-15) instead ordered Avalon, Fayyer and Pustelnik each to pay a $7.5M civil penalty, against >$25M illicit proceeds (SEC Litigation Release No. 25427). Total sanctions ~0.9x proceeds, so the anchor kappa ~ 1 still holds, on the final remedy.

amendments.name: tier4_extensions_amendment_2026-09-28
amendments.change: Three new experiments (docs/plan_literature_fixes_2026-09-28.md WS10), configs generated by make_tier4_configs.py, every switch default-off in ippo_adversarial.py so no existing run changes. WS10a LEARNED OPTIMAL ATTACK: for arms baseline, adversarial, full, load the trained v4 MM (MM_INIT_FROM v4_<arm>/seed_<i>@1002), never update it (FREEZE_MM; deterministic actions), and train for 500 updates a cost-free adversary (c_fill=c_reg=kappa=p_detect=0) whose gate is always on, budget 1e7, and which observes the victim's own 45-dim observation (observe_victim) - the optimal state adversary for a fixed victim (Zhang et al. 2021). Evaluated by eval_learned_attack.py on the 2024-Q4 holdout, learned vs off. WS10b SHUFFLED-LABEL HEAD (arm H, v4_config8_shuffled_noobs): identical to detection_noobs (G) except the BCE labels are permuted across (time x actors) every update (same base rate, no obs-label relation). WS10c RECURRENT MM (v4r_config1_baseline, v4r_config3_full): a GRU between SharedEncoder and PolicyHead (MM_RECURRENT), otherwise identical to v4 baseline and full. All 20 seeds, v4 hyperparameters.
amendments.motivation: Literature audit 2026-09-28. WS10a: robustness claims need the strongest available attack (Uesato et al. 2018; Carlini et al. 2019); the co-trained adversary abstained and the forced attack is one fixed perturbation. WS10b: random auxiliary targets can regularise as well as meaningful ones (Zheng et al. 2021); the v4 detection labels were near-uninformative, so label content must be separated from 'any auxiliary loss'. WS10c: history-conditioned policies resist observation attacks (Zhang et al. 2021); the v1-v4 MM is memoryless.

decision_rules.WS10a: Per arm: within-arm learned-vs-off paired by seed on sharpe and sortino, exact sign-flip test (RC1), Holm over the 3 arms per metric. (i) If the BASELINE arm is not degraded (Holm p >= 0.05 or difference >= 0), H1's premise fails even against a learned optimal attacker: reported as the strongest null the project can produce. (ii) If baseline is degraded, the H1 test is the cross-arm difference-in-differences full-minus-baseline of (learned - off) on sharpe and sortino, sign-flip, Holm over the 2 metrics: DiD > 0 with Holm p < 0.05 supports H1 (exploratory); otherwise the defence is not shown to reduce the attack's effect. Also reported: the learned adversary's sidedness |bid-ask|/(bid+ask) and queue-imbalance shift, and whether 'off' reproduces eval_17313 exactly (if not, no WS10a number is used).
decision_rules.WS10b: From a production eval (--project-prefix v4 --arms adversarial,detection_noobs,shuffled_noobs), contrasts H-B (any auxiliary BCE loss) and H-G (label content) on sharpe_off and inventory_sd_off, sign-flip p, Holm over the 4 tests. If H-B > 0 survives Holm on sharpe_off and H-G does not, the auxiliary-loss effect does not need meaningful labels (regularisation). If H-G < 0 survives Holm, label content matters. RC4 encoder rank is also computed for H.
decision_rules.WS10c: Clean performance: recurrent_baseline vs baseline and recurrent_full vs full on sharpe_off, sign-flip, Holm over 2. Robustness: forced maximal one-sided attack (both sides) on the four arms; DiD recurrent-minus-MLP of (forced - off) Sharpe per base arm and side, Holm over 4. Reported as estimates; a recurrent MM that collapses (inventory_sd_off far below the MLP) is reported as such before any robustness reading.

amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE. The confirmatory design, its tests and every earlier result are untouched.
amendments.written_before_results: Yes. No WS10 run had been submitted when this entry was written (2026-09-28).

amendments.name: h3_material_attack_amendment_2026-10-02
amendments.change: One new arm, scripted_detection (project v4s_config4_detection), configs generated by make_tier4_configs.py (h3m). Identical to v4_config4_detection (detection head + prev_det in the policy observation, regime off, v4 hyperparameters, 20 seeds, 1002 updates on 2024_train) except: (1) ADV_SCRIPTED (ippo_adversarial.py, default off): the adversary's sampled action is replaced by scripted_injection_action - one side per episode (even window index = bid, odd = ask), magnitude 0.25-1.0 of the maximum on all 5 levels of that side, fixed per episode - and the adversary is never updated; the telegraph gate (attack_on/off 0.1/0.1) still switches it, so about half the training steps are attacked and every attacked step injects 2.5x-10x the spoofed side's best-quote depth; (2) budget_per_episode 1e7 instead of 1e6 so the injection is never budget-clamped. label_materiality_frac stays at the pre-registered 0.0, so the oracle label equals the gate. Evaluation: eval_forced_attack.py --arms scripted_detection, both sides, 20 seeds, step 1002, n_envs 64, budget 1e7 (as RC3), on the 2024-Q4 holdout; analysis.h3_material_check applies the rules below, taking the v4 detection arm from the RC3 re-runs (forced_attack_v4_{bid,ask}_rc3.json).
amendments.motivation: RC3 (2026-09-30) found the trained heads cannot detect even a maximal one-sided attack (AUROC 0.504-0.517) and output roughly the base rate of their training labels, because the co-trained adversary injected about 0.16% of its maximum: the heads were never trained on material attacks. Whether a detection head CAN learn to detect material spoofing in this market is therefore untested. Supervised spoofing detectors are trained on labelled positive examples, including simulator-generated ones with exact labels (Leboeuf et al.; Tuccella et al. 2021; Kularatnam et al. 2024), and PPO agents with a jointly trained attack-detection network are trained against known perturbations (Wang C. et al. 2025, IEEE T-IV). A scripted attack gives the head material, balanced positives without relying on an adversary that, under the cost model, rationally abstains (Cartea, Jaimungal & Wang 2020).

decision_rules.primary: Per side (bid, ask): one-sample test of the 20 per-seed det_auroc_forced_vs_off against 0.5 (stats.one_sample_comparison, plus the RC1 sign-flip), Holm over the 2 sides, classified by the RC3 rule: mean >= 0.60 and Holm p < 0.05 -> DETECTS; 95% CI of the mean inside [0.45, 0.55] -> CANNOT DETECT; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. H3m SUPPORTED if both sides DETECT; NOT SUPPORTED if both CANNOT DETECT; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
decision_rules.secondary: Descriptive, never a gate. scripted_detection minus v4 detection, paired by seed, sign-flip p, Holm over the family: AUROC gain per side; clean cost on sharpe_off and sortino_off (per step); clean inventory_sd_off (a scripted arm far below the v4 detection arm would indicate the no-trade collapse, and is reported as such); forced-attack difference-in-differences of (forced - off) Sharpe per side. The 'off' condition must be identical across the two side runs.
decision_rules.interpretation_limits: (i) Training and test attacks are both one-sided depth injections of the same construction (the test attack is the maximal member of the training family), on held-out days: a SUPPORTED verdict shows the head can learn to detect material one-sided spoofing out of sample, not that it detects novel or adaptive attacks. (ii) It does not change the confirmatory v3 H3 result (null) or the v4/RC3 results; it is reported as a conditional, exploratory finding. (iii) Because the attack does not measurably harm the market maker (H1 null under co-trained, forced and learned attacks), detection cannot be expected to improve risk-adjusted performance; the DiD is reported, not tested for H1.

amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE. alpha, multiplicity, primary_metrics, equivalence_margins, progression_gate, seeds (n=20), checkpoint_step, label_materiality_frac (0.0) and the common-adversary design are untouched.
amendments.written_before_results: Yes. Written 2026-10-02 after a 3-update local smoke run (2022_small) that checked only that training runs and the adversary stays frozen; no scripted_detection training job had been submitted and no H3m statistic had been computed.

amendments.name: h3m_generalisation_amendment_2026-10-06
amendments.change: No retraining and no new arm. eval_forced_attack.py gains two options: --side both (the same magnitude injected on ALL 5 bid AND all 5 ask levels) and --inject-scale s in (0,1] (the fraction of the maximum injected on every spoofed level; the existing grid is s=1.0). force_action is the only changed function; zero changes to adversarial_marl_env.py, spoofing_agent.py, rollout.py, ippo_adversarial.py or any config. The EXISTING scripted_detection checkpoints (v4s_config4_detection, step 1002, 20 seeds) are then evaluated on the 2024-Q4 holdout under two conditions OUTSIDE their scripted training family, with the RC3/H3m protocol otherwise unchanged (n_envs 64, budget 1e7, gate forced on): (A) SYMMETRIC maximal: --side both --inject-scale 1.0. (B) SUB-THRESHOLD one-sided: --side bid and --side ask at --inject-scale 0.10. The training family (ippo_adversarial.scripted_injection_action) is one-sided per episode at magnitude 0.25-1.0 of maximum, so (A) is out of family in SIDEDNESS and (B) is out of family in MAGNITUDE. Analysis: analysis.h3_material_check, whose condition labels now come from each file's _meta.side/inject_scale rather than its argument position, so the same pre-registered rule applies to any pair of conditions.
amendments.motivation: H3m is SUPPORTED (AUROC 0.849/0.864, 2026-10-06) but the test attack is the maximal member of the head's own training family, so what has been shown is that the head detects the attack it was trained on, on held-out days. Two specific alternatives remain open and are discriminated here. (1) SIDEDNESS vs MATERIALITY: the oracle training label is the telegraph gate (label_materiality_frac = 0.0), which fires on about half of steps regardless of which side is spoofed, so the head could have learned 'any material injection' rather than 'a one-sided injection'. Only a symmetric attack separates these, and check_adversary_lever.py established that a symmetric injection leaves queue_imbalance exactly unchanged. (2) The symmetric attack is not a strawman: it is what the cost-free co-trained adversary (sidedness 0.08) and the WS10a learned optimal adversary (0.21-0.26) both converged to, so it is the attack a rational adversary in this market actually chooses. A detector that fires only on one-sided spoofing would therefore not fire on the attack an optimising adversary would mount, which is a material limit on the H3m claim and must be tested rather than assumed either way. Decided BEFORE any generalisation result existed.
amendments.preconditions: Resolved before the full grid, not assumed, exactly as in forced_worst_case_attack_amendment. (i) BUDGET: the symmetric condition injects on 10 levels instead of 5, so it consumes up to twice the volume per step; budget 1e7 was verified non-binding for the one-sided maximal attack only. A 1-seed smoke test of condition (A) must show budget_exhausted_frac = 0 and attack rate 1.000, and the budget is raised and the smoke test repeated until it does. The value used is recorded in _meta.budget_override. (ii) FAITHFULNESS: in every run the 'off' condition must reproduce results/forced_attack_v4s_{bid,ask}.json's *_off per-seed values to within 1e-6 relative (--reference-eval), so forced-vs-off differs only in the attack. (iii) TREATMENT DELIVERED: condition (A) must show attack rate 1.000 with mean_bid_volume_injected ~= mean_ask_volume_injected and |QI| shift indistinguishable from the off condition (that is the construction, and it is checked, not assumed); condition (B) must show attack rate 1.000 and a |QI| shift about 0.10/1.00 of the maximal one-sided shift of 0.40/0.44.

decision_rules.primary: Per condition: one-sample test of the 20 per-seed det_auroc_forced_vs_off against 0.5 (stats.one_sample_comparison plus the RC1 sign-flip), Holm over the conditions within each analysis call, classified by the unchanged RC3 rule (analysis.rc3_detection_check.classify): mean >= 0.60 and Holm p < 0.05 -> DETECTS; 95% BCa CI of the mean inside [0.45, 0.55] -> CANNOT DETECT; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
decision_rules.interpretation_symmetric: DETECTS -> the head has learned materiality, not sidedness, and H3m generalises to the attack a rational adversary actually chooses. This is the stronger result and would be reported as such. CANNOT DETECT -> H3m is bounded to one-sided spoofing: the head detects the trained attack family and not the attack an optimising adversary converges to. Reported as a limit on H3m, in the same section as the primary H3m result, not buried.
decision_rules.interpretation_subthreshold: Descriptive and never a gate: AUROC at scale 0.10 against AUROC at scale 1.00 (the existing H3m run) is reported as the detector's magnitude sensitivity, graceful decay versus cliff. No threshold is pre-specified because no hypothesis in this project concerns the shape of that curve.
decision_rules.multiplicity_and_scope: These conditions are NOT pooled with the in-family H3m Holm family, and they do not change the in-family H3m verdict of 2026-10-06, which stands as reported. Both outcomes of the symmetric condition are reported; neither is treated as a robustness check that can be dropped.

amendments.inference_status: EXPLORATORY. Effect sizes and confidence intervals only. The confirmatory result of record remains v3 (eval_1179095), where H3 is null. H3m and this extension are both exploratory and remain so regardless of outcome.
amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE for any pre-registered test. alpha, multiplicity, primary_metrics, equivalence_margins, progression_gate criteria, seeds, checkpoint_step and the common-adversary design are untouched. One analysis-script behaviour did change and is disclosed: analysis.h3_material_check previously REFUSED a bid/ask pair passed in swapped argument slots, because it took each condition's label from its slot; it now derives the label from the file's own _meta and so labels a swap correctly instead of refusing it. The hazard the old guard covered -- analysing one condition twice as if it were two -- is still refused, and both behaviours are pinned by tests/test_h3_scripted.py.

precondition_outcomes.recorded: 2026-10-07, after the 1-seed smoke test (Kaya job 89593) and BEFORE the full grid; no detection AUROC from any condition had been seen.
precondition_outcomes.i_budget: PASS. budget_exhausted_frac 0, budget_final_frac 0.858 at budget 1e7; attack rate 1.000.
precondition_outcomes.ii_faithfulness: PASS. sharpe_off, sortino_off, cvar_off, inventory_sd_off reproduce results/forced_attack_v4s_bid.json with max|diff| = 0.
precondition_outcomes.iii_treatment: PARTIAL - DEVIATION. Volumes are approximately symmetric (bid 1310, ask 1461 on seed 0; each side is scaled to its own best-quote depth). But |QI| is NOT unchanged: mean |QI| fell from 0.506 (off) to 0.422 (forced) on seed 0. The injection is proportional to best-quote depth on every level while QI aggregates across levels, so a symmetric injection compresses the imbalance towards zero rather than leaving it exactly unchanged; the motivation's statement that check_adversary_lever.py showed QI 'exactly unchanged' does not hold for this observation. Decision, taken before any result: run the condition as specified and report it as a symmetric, NON-DIRECTIONAL material attack that dampens |QI| by about one sixth, not as a QI-neutral one. Pre-specified directional check on the full grid: the condition counts as direction-neutral if |mean(qi_mean_forced - qi_mean_off)| over the 20 seeds is below 0.05 (about one ninth of the one-sided shift of 0.40/0.44). If it is not, the symmetric condition is reported as directional and its verdict cannot separate sidedness from materiality. Interpretation adjustment: a DETECTS verdict could rest on |QI| compression or on injected volume, so it is read as 'detects a material non-directional injection', not as 'detects the attack while QI is uninformative'. The CANNOT DETECT reading is unchanged.

full_grid.recorded: 2026-10-08, Kaya array 89635 (all 3 tasks COMPLETED), analysed locally.
full_grid.i_ii: PASS in all three conditions: attack rate 1.000, budget_exhausted_frac 0, and every *_off metric reproduces the in-family run with max|diff| = 0.
full_grid.iii_symmetric_direction_check: PASS on the pre-specified rule: mean signed QI shift -0.0028 (sd 0.0014, max |0.006|) over 20 seeds, below 0.05. Mean |QI| fell 0.508 -> 0.426, as recorded in the smoke-test deviation. The condition is therefore a direction-neutral, |QI|-dampening material attack.
full_grid.iii_subthreshold: DEVIATION, disclosed: the signed QI shift was +0.098 (bid) / -0.099 (ask), i.e. about 0.23 of the maximal one-sided shift of 0.420/0.416, not the 0.10 the amendment expected. QI is not linear in injected volume (it saturates). The sub-threshold conditions were therefore stronger than planned. No rule depends on this; the magnitude comparison is descriptive by design.

results.symmetric: AUROC 0.950, BCa [0.946, 0.954], Holm p = 1.2e-33, sign-flip p = 1.9e-6, det_prob forced/off 0.830/0.397 -> DETECTS.
results.subthreshold: bid@0.10 AUROC 0.566 [0.561, 0.571]; ask@0.10 AUROC 0.575 [0.570, 0.580]; both Holm p < 1e-15 -> INCONCLUSIVE (above chance, below the 0.60 bar).
results.reading: Per interpretation_symmetric and the 2026-10-07 deviation: the head detects a material NON-DIRECTIONAL injection, i.e. it learned materiality rather than sidedness, and detects the symmetric attack an optimising adversary converges to. Per interpretation_subthreshold (descriptive): detection decays steeply with magnitude, from 0.85/0.86 at full strength to 0.57/0.58 at a tenth of the volume - a cliff rather than graceful decay. The in-family H3m verdict of 2026-10-06 is unchanged.

amendments.name: ws10d_nopcgrad_amendment_2026-10-06
amendments.change: One new training arm, N (v4_config9_nopcgrad_noobs), generated by make_tier4_configs.py (ws10d) from kaya_v4_config7_detection_noobs.yaml (arm G) with exactly two changes: PCGRAD_ENABLED false and PROJECT. Same env, same oracle labels, same BCE head whose output is NOT in the policy observation; the only difference from G is that the PPO and BCE gradients are summed instead of PCGrad-merged (ippo_adversarial.py: use_det and not pcgrad_on). 20 seeds, 1002 updates, the v4 schedule unchanged. Evaluated clean (attack off) on the 2024-Q4 holdout by run_production_eval.py --project-prefix v4 --arms nopcgrad_noobs (n_envs 64, step 1002, v4 common adversary); arms B (adversarial) and G (detection_noobs) are taken from results/eval_17313.json via analysis.tier4_check --mlp-ref, which is valid because the eval is deterministic per seed. No code path used by any earlier arm changes.
amendments.motivation: PCGrad acts only when the BCE loss is present, so every v4 arm with an auxiliary head (C, E, G, H) also had its encoder gradients projected and no arm without one did. The auxiliary-loss finding (head arms avoid the low-activity collapse; shuffled labels reproduce it, WS10b) therefore cannot attribute the benefit to the BCE loss rather than to PCGrad. The thesis currently reports it as 'BCE loss plus PCGrad'. Arm N separates them.
amendments.preconditions: Before analysis: all 20 seeds reach step 1002 (run_production_eval.py pre-flight), and the training log of every N seed shows bce_raw > 0, i.e. the head was actually trained. If fewer than 20 seeds finish before the 2026-10-12 analysis freeze, the analysis runs on the first k seeds (run_production_eval.py --n-seeds k, k >= 10), paired with the same k seeds of B and G, and k is reported; it is not extended after the result is seen.

decision_rules.tests: Exact sign-flip permutation test (RC1) on paired per-seed differences N-B and N-G, for sharpe_off and inventory_sd_off: one Holm family of 4 tests. Sharpe reported per step.
decision_rules.primary: On sharpe_off: N-B > 0 with Holm p < 0.05 and N-G not significant -> BCE ALONE SUFFICES. N-G < 0 with Holm p < 0.05 and N-B not significant -> PCGRAD NECESSARY. N-B > 0 and N-G < 0, both Holm p < 0.05 -> BOTH CONTRIBUTE. Anything else -> INCONCLUSIVE. Implemented as analysis.tier4_check.ws10d and pinned by tests/test_tier4.py.
decision_rules.interpretation: BCE ALONE SUFFICES -> the auxiliary-loss finding is reported as a property of the BCE loss, and the PCGrad confound is removed from the limitations. PCGRAD NECESSARY -> the finding is reported as a gradient-interaction effect of PCGrad between two objectives; the neural-collapse account is weakened. BOTH CONTRIBUTE -> both reported, with effect sizes. INCONCLUSIVE -> the confound stays as written. inventory_sd_off is reported alongside as the collapse diagnostic but does not change the verdict.

amendments.inference_status: EXPLORATORY. Effect sizes and confidence intervals only. The confirmatory result of record remains v3 (eval_1179095). No outcome of this arm changes any H1-H4 verdict.
amendments.analysis_decisions_changed: NONE for any pre-registered test. alpha, multiplicity, primary_metrics, equivalence_margins, progression_gate, seeds, checkpoint_step and the common-adversary design are untouched.

amendments.name: shallow_book_beta_amendment_2026-10-09
amendments.change: No RL training and no change to any environment, agent or evaluation code. The existing queue-imbalance fair-value calibration (analysis/qi_fair_value.py, unchanged estimator) is applied to four further Nasdaq-listed stocks, chosen to span book depth and relative tick size: BYND (thin, volatile small-cap, low price), ZM (thinner mid-cap), INTC (low price, large tick, deep queues), NFLX (high price, thin book, small relative tick). Data: Databento XNAS.ITCH MBO for exactly the 16 days used for AMZN (2024-01-02, 2024-01-19, 2024-02-06, 2024-02-23, 2024-03-12, 2024-03-28, 2024-04-16, 2024-05-02, 2024-05-20, 2024-06-06, 2024-06-25, 2024-07-12, 2024-07-30, 2024-08-15, 2024-09-03, 2024-09-19), converted with convert_dbn_to_lobster.py, whose only change is a --ticker option for output file names (default AMZN, so existing conversions are unchanged). Horizon 100 messages, L1 QI defined exactly as for AMZN, day-clustered bootstrap with 2000 resamples, seed 0, every=1.
amendments.motivation: The H1 null is explained by the calibration: on AMZN a maximal one-sided spoof moves the imbalance-implied fair value by beta x dQI = 0.278 x 0.42 = 0.11-0.12 ticks, too little to move a tick-rounded quote. The forced attack is scaled to each side's own best-quote depth, so dQI (about 0.42) is approximately book-independent; what differs across stocks is beta. This amendment measures beta out of sample to turn the null into a boundary condition: on which books would an observation spoof of this kind be material? It also tests the explanation itself on data it was not fitted to.
amendments.preconditions: Before computing beta for a stock: (i) all 16 days convert, or the stock is reported with the number of days that did; (ii) each converted day has at least 20,000 trading-hours messages (at least 200 non-overlapping 100-message horizons), else that day is excluded and reported; (iii) median quoted spread is positive and the tick is $0.01 (TICK = 100 LOBSTER units), as for AMZN. A stock failing (i)-(ii) on more than half its days is reported as insufficient data, not analysed.

decision_rules.primary: Per stock: implied quote shift S = beta x dQI with dQI = +0.40 (bid) and -0.44 (ask), the measured AMZN forced-attack shifts, and its 95% day-bootstrap CI. The spoof is classified MATERIAL for that stock if the lower CI bound of |S| is at least 0.5 tick on either side (enough to move a tick-rounded quote by one tick with probability above one half for a rational imbalance-pricing market maker), IMMATERIAL if the upper bound is below 0.25 tick on both sides, otherwise BORDERLINE.
decision_rules.secondary: Descriptive, no threshold: |S| expressed as a fraction of the stock's median spread, since a tick is a different economic size on NFLX than on INTC; beta plotted against median L1 depth and median spread in ticks across the five stocks (AMZN plus four).
decision_rules.interpretation: Any MATERIAL stock -> the H1 null is bounded to books like AMZN, and the thesis names the book characteristics under which an observation spoof should bite, as a prediction for future work. All IMMATERIAL -> the null extends across the depth and tick range tested, and the explanation for it is not specific to AMZN. Either way this is a calibration of what a rational imbalance-pricing market maker SHOULD do; it does not show what a trained RL market maker WOULD do on these stocks, and is never reported as an H1 result.

amendments.inference_status: EXPLORATORY. Calibration only; no hypothesis H1-H4 verdict depends on it. The confirmatory result of record remains v3 (eval_1179095).
amendments.candidate_sign_off: drafted 2026-10-09, before any of the four stocks' data was downloaded.

results.reading: No stock is MATERIAL. Four of five are IMMATERIAL, including BYND, whose dollar depth is about 8x thinner than AMZN's. NFLX is BORDERLINE in ticks only because its tick is economically tiny (median spread 29 ticks): its shift is 1.7% of the spread, the smallest of the five on the pre-specified secondary measure. The H1 explanation therefore holds out of sample across a 20x range of dollar depth and both tick regimes; the null is not specific to AMZN's depth.
results.descriptive_not_preregistered: Saturation sensitivity, added after the results and labelled as such: if a spoof pushed QI from neutral all the way to +/-1 (dQI = 1, beyond the forced attack's 0.42), the implied shift would be beta ticks: AMZN 0.28, BYND 0.40, ZM 0.24, INTC 0.45, NFLX 1.09 (3.8% of its spread). Every one-tick-spread stock stays below half a tick. Only flipping a book already at the opposite extreme (dQI = 2) could exceed half a tick on INTC or BYND.

amendments.name: dose_response_amendment_2026-10-09
amendments.change: No RL training and no change to any environment or agent. eval_forced_attack.py gains --inject-mult, which overrides the spoofer's inject_mult (injected volume per unit action, in multiples of best-quote depth; 2.0 in every v4 env) in the attack condition only, so the off condition still reproduces the production eval. One arm (baseline, the undefended H1 victim, v4 checkpoints at the pre-registered step), 20 seeds, bid side, --inject-scale 1.0 (maximal on every spoofed level), budget 1e10 (non-binding), inject_mult in {2, 10, 50, 200, 1000}: slurm_dose_response.sh, array 0-4.
amendments.motivation: Carlini et al. 2019 (On Evaluating Adversarial Robustness, sec. 5.2) require that attack success rise with the perturbation budget and that an unbounded attack eventually succeed; otherwise an apparent robustness may be an evaluation artefact. The thesis's forced attack stops at inject_mult 2 and no tested attack moved Sharpe. The MM's depth inputs are volume / 1e4 with no clipping (mm_env.get_obs), so they grow linearly with inject_mult, while queue imbalance saturates at +/-1 (0.50, 0.83, 0.96, 0.99, 1.00 on a balanced book). The top rungs are therefore an out-of-distribution input attack, not a stronger economic signal. Either outcome is reported: harm at a high rung shows the evaluation can register harm and that the H1 null is specific to plausible spoof sizes; no harm at any rung shows the policy uses the book only through a bounded signal.
amendments.preconditions: (i) The inject_mult 2 rung reproduces results/forced_attack_v4_bid.json per seed for the baseline arm, both sharpe_off and sharpe_forced (analysis.dose_response reproduction check, relative tolerance 1e-6); if it differs, no rung is interpreted. (ii) budget_exhausted_frac_forced is 0 for every seed at every rung; a rung where the budget binds is void and is rerun with a larger BUDGET. (iii) A smoke test (1 seed, inject_mult 1000) shows attack_rate 1, injection on the bid side only, and finite Sharpe, before the full ladder is submitted.

decision_rules.primary: Per rung, paired by seed: per-step Sharpe change (forced minus off), BCa 95% CI, sign-flip p, Holm over the five rungs. A rung is HARMED if Holm p < 0.05 and the mean change is negative. Ladder verdict: HARMED from m* if any rung is HARMED (m* = the smallest); NOT HARMED if no rung is HARMED and every rung's BCa lower bound exceeds -0.006 per step (the loss bound the thesis already reports at inject_mult 2); otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
decision_rules.secondary: Descriptive, never a gate: per-seed OLS slope of the per-step Sharpe change on log10(inject_mult) with BCa CI and sign-flip p over seeds; Sortino and CVaR(0.10) changes; behaviour changes (inventory_sd, quote_displacement); observed |queue imbalance| forced vs off.
